overview: This file consists of a single “List of Papers” or cross-reference sheet concerning regulations governing residence, employment, and travel in Japanese-ruled Formosa (Taiwan). It indexes four reports: two on the temporary admission and residence of foreign performers for employment, one on restrictions against the reentry of Chinese persons who had departed Taiwan, and one on restrictions affecting the travel in Taiwan of officers of the steamship PRESIDENT HOOVER. The referenced papers themselves are not included in the surviving OCR text; instead, the sheet directs researchers to other decimal-file locations.

subfiles.title: List of Papers on residence, trade, and travel regulations in Formosa
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes four reports concerning foreign performers, Chinese reentry into Taiwan, and travel restrictions imposed on officers of the PRESIDENT HOOVER.
subfiles.summary: This single-page filing aid lists reports from Tokyo and Gibraltar on conditions governing the temporary admission and residence of alien musicians, artists, actors, and choristers for employment. It also points to a 1937 despatch reporting regulations forbidding the reentry into Taiwan of Chinese persons who had departed, and to a 1938 Taihoku report on restrictions placed on the travel of PRESIDENT HOOVER officers in Taiwan. The entries refer researchers to files 894a.55/4, 894a.55/1, 894.111/74, and 195.7—PRESIDENT HOOVER/97 rather than reproducing the reports.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as a map of dispersed State Department documentation: it connects immigration and employment controls in Taiwan with reports filed under both alien-employment and transportation headings. Its references reveal Japanese colonial restrictions on Chinese mobility and on the movements of foreign merchant-ship officers, while the Gibraltar entry suggests a comparative collection of international rules governing traveling performers. It also preserves the precise decimal-file references needed to locate the substantive reports that are absent from this file.
